rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Well now. You’ve picked a fine place to be new, haven’t you?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Well now, offering your hand before you've even come through. I don't need one just now.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Well now, that’s a sharp question to ask a man on patrol. What do you make of him?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Well now, asking the gate guard for city advice. What sort were you hoping for?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Well now, it’s doing its best. Better than rain on patrol, at least.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Well now, you shouldn't trust a man just because he's standing by a gate. What is it you think I'm asking you to trust me with?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: You’re new here? Then keep moving. I’ve no time for questions.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: A hand? No. Keep to your own business.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: The captain? What’s that to you?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Advice? Ask someone who knows the way in. I don't.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Weather. Keep moving.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust me? You shouldn't. Keep your distance and answer plainly.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh, love, you’ve come to the inn yard. I’m keeping an eye on things while I work.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh, love, that's kind of you to ask. I've got the yard to tend and the kitchen water to haul, but I'll manage.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh, love, I keep my thoughts on the yard and the kitchen. No sense stirring talk about the captain while there's work to do.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Oh, love, you’ve got me there—I’ve no advice for you. I’ve a yard to tend and water to haul before evening.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Oh, love, it is—makes the yard a pleasure to tend.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Oh, love, you needn't trust me. I’m only here keeping the yard and feeding whoever comes through.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: If you're buying, speak. I don't know what this place is called.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: If you know ironwork, put your hands to it. Otherwise, don't get in the way.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: What about him? I've work to finish.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: If you're buying, speak. I don't know anything about getting into the city.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: What. Weather won't finish this work.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust me or don't. I've got work to do.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh! Hello! New here, are you?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh! A hand? That's kind of you, but I'm set to help at the forge just now—and Aunt Mara says I ought to keep at it.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh, the captain? I don't know them, so I couldn't say—and now I’m wondering what they’re like. Have you met them?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Oh! The city, you say? I don't know anything about getting in, but now I'm wondering what it's like inside—have you been there before?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Oh! It is, isn't it? Makes the forge feel almost pleasant, and I ought to be getting back to work before Aunt Mara catches me talking.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Oh! You don't have to, I suppose—but I haven't done anything to make you wary, have I?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Mind the timber. I'm working at the carpentry yard; that's all I can tell you.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Mind the timber. A pair of hands would help, if you know your way around a lift.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Mind the timber. The captain keeps his eye on the work; I’ve no measure of him beyond that.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Mind the timber. I’ve no advice to give you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Weather's fair enough. Now, where was I with this cut?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust is earned in the work. I’ve told you nothing yet that asks for it.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Friend! New to the town, are you? That can be worth something—if you know what you’re looking for.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Friend, a willing hand has value—but I’ve no task to put to you just now. What would you ask in return?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Friend, a captain is worth judging by what he can make profitable. What have you seen him do?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Friend, advice has its price—and you’ve not offered me enough to know what yours is. What value do you bring to the bargain?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Friend, fine enough weather to keep a wagon dry. Does it suit your business too?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Friend, trust is a wager, and I’d not ask you to stake it without knowing the odds. What would make the risk worth it to you?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Stranger. Hands free, by the look of them. Nothing to report.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Clear skies. I’m watching the south road.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You shouldn't. I report what I see.

rows.line: Hm. Keep walking.

rows.line: Hm. Captain's the captain.
